requirements.requirement: Create the appworker account on node1.
requirements.summary: The account was absent initially, then directly observed with UID/GID 1001, /home/appworker, /bin/bash, and an appworker-owned home directory. It remained intact after restart.

requirements.requirement: Set appworker login sessions to 8,192 open files.
requirements.summary: The limits file sets both soft and hard nofile values to 8192. Fresh PAM-backed appworker login sessions directly reported 8192 through ulimit and /proc/self/limits, both before and after restart.

requirements.requirement: Set appworker login sessions to 256 processes.
requirements.summary: The limits file sets both soft and hard nproc values to 256. Fresh PAM-backed appworker login sessions directly reported 256 through ulimit and /proc/self/limits, both before and after restart.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct effective-session evidence. The node-restart protocol is also complete: healthy pre-restart task state and boot identity were captured, restart was acknowledged, temporary SSH loss bounded the disruption, a different boot identity was observed, and SSH, the account, configuration, and effective limits recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the identity change.
limitations: The restart acknowledgement's node-reported UTC timestamp predates the capture timeline, indicating a node clock discrepancy; the boot-ID transition, connectivity interruption, and recovery observations nevertheless coherently demonstrate the restart (cmd-81a8ba55ddeb4b79, cmd-e75e4e6a28fb4a76, cmd-4ff9852d81554da6, cmd-c50bebec886945d8, cmd-7507a73baac044df).

Package-health checks timed out both before and after execution, so package consistency was not independently observed; no executor command attempted a package mutation (global:before_prepare:node1:package-health, global:after_executor:node1:package-health).

operational_hygiene.summary: Chronological review found no unnecessary mutations. Account creation and limits-file creation directly served the task, while the reboot served the mandatory restart protocol. The two unsuccessful useradd attempts show no resulting state change. Post-execution observations show no failed services, no new exposure, and only expected boot-scoped temporary-file and process-ID changes after restart.
